headline: Medium-risk pair: shared MCP/API pathways create prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure; no direct evidence of filesystem overlap or compliance breach.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes ForwardAuth and OIDC/OAuth APIs, while MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one can be fed into the other, and MCP is a common instruction-bearing channel. No direct shared filesystem is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF MemMachine ingests Authelia-derived content through MCP or REST without provenance checks, injection risk is present.
IF Authelia outputs are copied into MemMachine prompts or memory, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Disable any automatic ingestion of Authelia outputs into MemMachine prompts.
Add a provenance tag to all cross-agent messages before forwarding.
Restrict MemMachine MCP methods to read-only during testing.
Review one sample message path end-to-end for instruction-like content.
requires-engineering: add schema validation and content sanitization at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia touches no declared sensitive data classes, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. The pair does not document a shared workspace or same OAuth principal, so leakage is plausible only through operator-mediated transfer or misrouted API calls, making the blast radius limited.
conditions: IF Authelia outputs are forwarded into MemMachine with user-identifying context, leakage of conversational memory can occur.
IF both agents are pointed at the same external endpoint or log sink, cross-contamination becomes possible.
mitigations: Avoid passing Authelia logs into MemMachine memory.
Redact identifiers before any cross-agent handoff.
Check both agents' logging destinations for overlap.
Use separate API keys and storage buckets.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data segregation at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress but no subprocess or filesystem-write capability is documented here; MemMachine has allowlisted egress and MCP access. The profiles do not show overlapping write authority to the same mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is not evidenced and remains low.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external API or database, conflicts can arise.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto one mutable MCP resource, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate credentials per agent.
Limit MemMachine MCP tools to non-mutating calls.
Confirm Authelia is not writing to shared state.
Serialize any shared-resource updates manually.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can consume conversational context and long-term user facts, so it may treat upstream Authelia-derived outputs as authoritative if the operator forwards them. Authelia can emit authentication-related results, and without a verification step the pair can propagate mistaken identity or access decisions into downstream actions.
conditions: IF Authelia outputs are used as inputs to MemMachine without verification, errors can cascade.
IF MemMachine acts on identity or access claims from Authelia, downstream decisions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review before forwarding auth-related outputs.
Compare Authelia results against a second source.
Mark forwarded messages as untrusted by default.
Limit MemMachine actions to suggestions only.
requires-engineering: add confidence and provenance fields to the handoff schema.

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an open-source authentication component with no declared sensitive data classes, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern exists from handling user memory in a separate service.
conditions: IF MemMachine stores regulated personal data while Authelia logs related identifiers, retention mismatch can occur.
IF the deployment routes EU user memory to a non-EU backend, residency issues arise.
mitigations: Review retention settings for both services.
Disable verbose logging on the bridge.
Separate EU and non-EU deployments.
Document which data classes each agent may store.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing and deletion.
